## Design

### 2026-10-05 – October 5th, Morning

**2.5h**

October 5th, Morning

This morning, I started to work on the connection interface for the MCU carrier boards. I initially wanted to use m.2 connectors, and I think I will persue that in the future, but for now I went with a simple 2x10 pin header. For my first version, the IO will be fairly limited becasue I have to connect everything with only 20 pins, so I went with the bare minimum:
- SPI breakout
- I2C breakout
- 2 ADC pins
- 3 extra gpio pins
- 5v, 3v, and ground
- boot/reset
- usb
- user LED

This first version will only support USB capable microcontrollers, however If i continue this project in the future I will likely add a usb to seriel converter as well.

### 2026-10-06 – PCB Schematic

**2.5h**

PCB Schematic

Since yesterday morning, I started and finished the schematic for the base board. I picked a pretty simple voltage regulator, the AP2112K, for taking the 5v from usb and making it to 3.3v. I also picked micro usb for the first version because it's a little easier to implement and easier to hand solder. I included 3 leds, 1 for the 5v bus, 1 for the 3.3v bus, and one user led. I made sure to include testpoints for important signals and added mounting holes just in case.
